newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees sugar production down in 1996-97.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees sugar production down in 1996-97.

text.p: Philippine raw sugar output for the 1996-97 crop year ending August 31 is likely to fall to 1.8 million tonnes from the earlier forecast of 1.9 million due to damage wrought by typhoons late last year, the state-run Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) said on Tuesday.
SRA administrator Wilson Gamboa told a news conference heavy rains from the typhoons are likely to affect sugar harvests in the central Visayas island.
Too much water affects the sucrose content of the cane, he said.
"We are in fact revising our 1996-97 target due to typhoon damage in western Visayas island last year," Gamboa said.
"I don't expect us (the Philippines) producing more than 1.8 million tonnes in the current crop year," he added.
Western Visayas accounts for 54 percent of the estimated 370,000 hectares of land planted to sugar in the country.
"The typhoons damaged between 20 and 25 percent of total sugar land in western Visayas," Gamboa said.
Gamboa also told reporters that he expected the present sugar glut in the country due to overimportation from September 1995 to July 1996 to be mopped up by August this year.

He said he expected local raw sugar prices to improve in August this year when the glut would have been wiped out. A 50-kg bag of raw sugar is currently pegged at 540 pesos compared to 700 to 800 pesos at the start of 1996.

Gamboa said he expected total sugar available in 1996-97 at 2.528 million tonnes, including 686,000 tonnes in stock at the beginning of the crop year and the minimum 43,000 tonnes which has to be imported under World Trade Organisation laws.
Consumption in 1996-97 is forecast at 2.15 million tonnes, including 250,000 tonnes contracted exports to the United States.
"Sugar stocks at the end of crop year 1996-1997 is estimated at 378,000 tonnes, just enough to meet the 350,000-tonne two month starting inventory for crop year 1997-1998," he said.
In 1997-98, Gamboa said output would fall to 1.7 million tonnes as farmers switched to other crops because of the current glut.

Gamboa said he expected total sugar available in crop year 1997-1998 at 2.123 million tonnes while demand was placed at 2.25 million tonnes, including the projected 250,000 tonnes in sugar exports to the United States.
The Philippines is a beneficiary of a programme where the United States import sugar from developing countries at premium prices.

Gamboa said he expected a shortfall of 477,000-487,000 tonnes in the 1997-1998 given the required buffer of around 350,000 tonnes at the end of crop year 1997-1998 and the projected demand-supply gap of 127,000-137,000 tonnes.
